name: ether.fi AtomicQueue unauthenticated solver
summary: AtomicQueue.solve takes the solver as a caller-supplied argument and pulls the want token from it via transferFrom without requiring solver == msg.sender. The attacker registered its own request with a worthless offer token and an atomicPrice equal to each victim's balance, then named third-party wallets holding standing liquidETH or USDC allowances to the queue as solvers, draining them. Copycats repeated it within two hours against sETHFI, weETHs, eEIGEN, liquidUSD and liquidElixir allowances.
notes: Immutable AtomicQueue runtime with no owner or settable state other than user requests; solve's missing solver authentication exists from deployment.

Exact gross depletion of 62 third-party allowance holders across source-1 and eight later copycat transactions (source-7); worthless fake offer tokens credited to victims are not netted. Liquid assets use DefiLlama quotes; liquidElixir (no quote) uses realised proceeds of the last copycat's disposal, so the aggregate method is other. The first attacker's realised 15.4536 ETH from liquidETH does not set the liquidETH valuation.
